assumptions.statement: Households will keep a pantry inventory up to date manually or via low-effort input.
assumptions.rationale: Users explicitly state they will quit if inventory entry requires typing.

assumptions.statement: Households want automated weekly dinner plans combined with inventory tracking.
assumptions.rationale: Decision fatigue is widespread, but some users prefer manual planning or distrust automation.

assumptions.statement: Users will pay a monthly subscription fee for PantryPal.
assumptions.rationale: Many users expect free ad-supported versions or low fees, limiting willingness to pay.

assumptions.statement: PantryPal can solve household shopping coordination and reduce food waste.
assumptions.rationale: Food waste is a real pain point, but actual behaviour change through an app is unproven.

experiments.hypothesis: Users will complete a low-effort inventory input method without churning during the first week.
experiments.method: Ask 20 target households to test a prototype receipt or photo scanner interface for one week and track daily inventory updates.
experiments.success_metric: At least 70 percent of participants log inventory and return to update it at least twice during the week.

experiments.hypothesis: Users are willing to pay EUR 4.99 per month after experiencing grocery savings.
experiments.method: Run a landing page test presenting free versus premium pricing tiers to 500 targeted visitors.
experiments.success_metric: At least 5 percent click through and enter payment details.

open_questions: What are the country, income levels, and recruitment methods of the participants?
How do users behave over time regarding long-term usage and measured waste?
How do users prefer to input their inventory (photo, barcode, receipt, or online order history)?
Do users keep planning after week one?
What is the competitor traction, user base, ratings, and churn rate?
What is the specific market size for the target segment?
Who in the household actually decides what to eat and who pays for the subscription?
recommendation_reason: While decision fatigue and food waste are validated problems, the high usability risk of inventory maintenance and uncertainty around subscription willingness to pay require targeted testing before full development.
